status: THE DRESSED GAUGE GATE ON THE DIRECTED-LINK NETWORK, AND THE QUINTET DISPERSION. Part A (the V79 open step, split by computation): the directed-link Gauss charge closes ONLY with the conjugate head convention (tail +L, head -Lbar) - the naive chain sign convention leaks 4.8e+00 on the two-link star (T1); the bare bond gate leaks the vertex charge 1.92 (T2); the Kogut-Susskind ELECTRIC gate exp(i g10 C_x^2) is exactly gauge-invariant (max over all 45 charges 6.0e-15) and its spectrum IS the V79 content theorem, phases g10 x {45, 85, 117} with multiplicities 32, 288, 1120 (T3); every two-site dressed-hopping candidate on the fixed adjoint link leaks (min 1.25e+01) - the invariant hopping needs a regular-representation link (T4). Part B (the V138 T5 escape route, run): on the directional network the flux is the link orientation (a c-number), the dressed hop exists exactly, and the step M(q) = exp(-i g10 sin(q).J) is unitary and O_h-covariant (improper elements invert the step: the network is chiral, T5). At GAMMA it is the identity: six gapless bands with content A1g + Eg + T2g - the quintet is present where the qubit link never had Eg (T6). Its dispersion is massless, linear (exponent 1.00), EXACTLY isotropic to leading order (direction spread O(eps^2)), with the helicity ladder speeds {0, g10, 2 g10} - the m = 0 branch and the A1g trace do not propagate - and UV-bounded by 2 g10 sqrt(3) (T7). VERDICT: the directional bond layer supplies the kinematics the qubit link was proved not to have (V138: no Eg, flat bands; V139: anisotropy 0.857): a massless, linear, isotropic quintet at the zone centre. What is NOT derived: the directional network's gauge group is the lattice direction group O_h, not Spin(10); the Spin(10)-invariant dressed hopping is obstructed on the fixed adjoint link (T4); the ladder speeds g10 x {1,2} = {0.2, 0.4} are not 1 (the dressing angle per hop is an input); the coupling of the quintet to the matter layer and the non-linear completion are not constructed.
